title: finding(i18n): check-i18n-dead-keys reports 28 LIVE `chatbot.tool.*` keys as CONFIRMED — the key template lives in a helper, not at the call site
body:
A third blind-spot class in `scripts/check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs`, sibling to #6666 but **not covered by its remedy**. Measured on `origin/main` `24135aba1`, which contains the #6666 fix (`2878cede4`, `propertyChainProbe()`).

## The claim

All 30 `chatbot.tool.*` keys are LIVE and rendering in shipping UI. 28 of them sit in **CONFIRMED**, the tier the script's own header calls the strongest and safest to delete. They are 28 of the 142 CONFIRMED entries — **19.7% of the whole top tier is one false-positive block**.

Deleting them would remove 300 translated strings (30 keys x 10 packs) and silently revert every AI copilot tool card to English in all nine non-English locales — the exact regression cloud#1658 was filed for and objectui#7254 fixed.

## Why both legs are blind — a new class

The consumer never spells the key. `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/tool-display.ts`:

```ts
export function toolTitleKey(name: string): string {
  return `chatbot.tool.${String(name).trim()}`;
}
// …
return translate ? translate(toolTitleKey(trimmed), english) : english;
```

The template that builds the key lives **inside a helper function**, so at the `t()`/`tt()`-shaped call site the key argument is a **function call, not a template literal**. In `analyze()` (`check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs`) both `dynamicHeads` (line 1879) and `dynamicFamilies` (line 1887) are populated only from `staticHead(argument)` / `templateShape(argument)` on an observed template-literal argument. A helper call yields neither.

Consequence, leg by leg:

| leg | sees it? | why |
|---|---|---|
| AST `referencedKeys` | no | no literal key at any call site |
| AST `dynamicHeads` | no | the template is in the helper; the argument is a call expression |
| full-key `textFootprint()` | no | the dotted key is never spelled |
| `propertyChainProbe()` (#6666) | no | `.tool.add_field` is spelled nowhere — the pack is not imported as an object here |

This is distinct from both classes the header enumerates. `LoadingScreen.tsx` is pack-object + property access (covered by design). `outboundAgentText.ts` is pack-object + dynamic index (covered by neither leg, but its four keys land in NEEDS-REVIEW **by luck**, via a nearby type union). This class has no such luck: 28 of 30 land in CONFIRMED. The 2 exceptions (`describe_object`, `visualize_data`) are demoted only because `tool-display-i18n.test.ts` happens to spell those two dotted keys as literals — the same luck, and it covers 2 of 30.

## Evidence

**1. Live call sites.** `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/ChatbotEnhanced.tsx`, both passing `tt = useSafeTranslate()` (line 1471):
- `:2079` `const friendlyTitle = humanizeToolName(tool.toolName, tt);` — the tool card header
- `:3127` `groups={summarizeTools(summaryTools, tt)}` — the activity chips, via `summarizeTools` (`:1281`)

**2. Exact registry correspondence.** The pack's 30 `chatbot.tool` leaves are **set-identical** to `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` in `@objectstack/spec` (`service-ai` 6 + `service-ai-studio` 24). No key without a tool, no tool without a key. Every key is the runtime target of `toolTitleKey(tool.toolName)` for a tool the platform actually ships.

**3. Ablation.** Removing `apply_edit: '应用修改'` from `packages/i18n/src/locales/zh.ts` (mutation confirmed on disk, blob `495a321a4` to `382253a89`; restored, `git diff HEAD` empty) turns the existing rendering pin RED:

```
FAIL |dom| packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/toolCardI18n-7254.test.tsx
TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element with the text: 应用修改
                                Apply edit
```

So one CONFIRMED key already breaks a shipping test on deletion. The pin covers 2 of 30.

**4. The forward gate is blind too — controlled pair, same file, same namespace, one level apart.**

| leg | mutation on `en.ts` | `check:i18n-keys` |
|---|---|---|
| A | delete `chatbot.tool.apply_edit` | **exit 0, GREEN** — pack count silently 2962 to 2961, still declares "every in-scope call-site key resolves" |
| B | delete `chatbot.toolState.completed` | **exit 1, RED** — `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx:1486:49 [missing-key]` |

B proves the gate is sensitive; A proves it is blind to this subtree. Nothing in CI would catch the deletion of 28 of these 30 keys.

## Suggested remedy (not implemented here — out of the reporting slice's scope)

`chatbot.tool.` is a textbook dynamic key family with a **closed, external, authoritative vocabulary** (`PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES`), which is exactly what `DYNAMIC_KEY_FAMILIES` (#4964) exists to describe. Two independent pieces are needed and neither works alone:

1. Let a family be declared against a helper-built head, since `dynamicHeads`/`dynamicFamilies` are observation-only today and record nothing for this shape.
2. `check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs` destructures only `referencedKeys, referencedBranches, dynamicHeads` from `analyze()` (line 373) — it never reads `dynamicFamilies`. So even a correctly declared family would **not** protect its members from the reverse sweep until the dead-key script consumes the declared registry as well.

A cheaper interim guard, independent of the above: pin the set-identity asserted in evidence 2 — every `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` member has a `chatbot.tool.` key and vice versa. That makes the whole subtree's liveness mechanical rather than a matter of a reader noticing.

## Scope note

Filed from the `chatbot.tool` slice of #4730, which **shipped zero diff** as a result: the dispatched deletion target turned out to be entirely live. No pack was edited; all mutations above were ablations, restored and verified byte-identical to their `HEAD` blob.
